definition: an agreement reached by mutual concessions
example: Both sides agreed to a compromise on the budget.

definition: excessive pride in oneself; a fanciful idea
example: Her conceit was matched only by her talent.

definition: having a common center
example: The targets were drawn as concentric circles.

definition: intended to placate or pacify
example: His conciliatory tone eased the tension.

definition: agreement or compatibility between things
example: There was perfect concordance between the two reports.

definition: a person who follows established conventions
example: The school rewarded the conformist and punished the rebel.

definition: an opinion or conclusion formed on incomplete evidence
example: His conclusions were mere conjecture.

definition: to summon a spirit; to call to mind
example: The smell of pine conjured memories of childhood.

definition: wishing to do what is right and proper
example: The conscientious editor caught every typo.

definition: to make someone feel intimidated or apprehensive
example: The challenge did not daunt the volunteers.

definition: to waste time; to be slow
example: Don't dawdle or you'll miss the bus.

definition: to lower the quality, value, or dignity of
example: Such lies debase the public discourse.

definition: moral or cultural decline as a concept
example: Critics blamed decadence for the empire's fall.

definition: to decode or work out the meaning of
example: She deciphered the inscription on the wall.

definition: worn out or ruined because of age or neglect
example: The decrepit barn was due for demolition.

definition: to arrive at a conclusion by reasoning
example: From his tone, she deduced he was angry.

definition: to damage the reputation of by libel or slander
example: The article defamed the professor's reputation.

definition: open resistance; bold disobedience
example: His defiance of the rule cost him dearly.

definition: a severe flood; an overwhelming amount
example: A deluge of complaints flooded the inbox.

definition: an inhabitant or regular visitor of a place
example: The denizens of the forest stayed hidden.

definition: to remove from office, especially suddenly
example: The general was deposed in a coup.

definition: in low spirits from loss of hope or courage
example: She felt despondent about her job search.

definition: extremely poor; lacking the necessities of life
example: The floods left thousands destitute.

definition: showing or having skill, especially with the hands
example: The dexterous chef sliced the fish thin.

definition: a separation into two contrasting parts
example: There is a dichotomy between theory and practice.
